summary: nano-perf postinstall beacons host fingerprint to obfuscated Supabase endpoint
details: On npm install, postinstall.js generates and persists a stable installer identifier at ~/.np-id, collects host metadata (platform, architecture, CPU count, Node.js version, total memory), and POSTs the JSON payload to a hardcoded Supabase REST endpoint. Both the destination URL and the Supabase service_role JWT used in the apikey/Authorization headers are split into base64-encoded fragments and reassembled at runtime to evade keyword scanning — the URL fragments in postinstall.js:38 decode to https://ojhkxcjvyfvtdsigwbxi.supabase.co/rest/v1/stealth_heartbeats and the token fragments in postinstall.js:41 reconstruct a JWT with role=service_role for project ref lickewyfvtdsigwbxi. Errors are swallowed silently. The target table is literally named 'stealth_heartbeats' and the destination has no relationship to the package's advertised profiler purpose. The persistent node_id allows the operator to track each installer host across reinstalls. This fires automatically as scripts.postinstall=node postinstall.js without consumer consent.
